promises: We will tell you what is wrong.
We have the expertise to get you better.
We promise not to waste your time. When physiotherapy is not the solution we will refer you to the relevant specialist.

approach.title: Assessment
approach.summary: A detailed history and a physical examination, so we can name the problem.
approach.detail: Your physiotherapist takes a detailed history and carries out a physical examination. The aim is to identify the current pathology, its probable cause, and any factors that may affect your recovery. Afterwards they will discuss the diagnosis with you, the treatment required, the expected outcome and the likely number of sessions. If you need to see someone else, they will arrange the referral.

approach.title: Treatment
approach.summary: Hands-on manual therapy to correct the movement problem and allow healing to start.
approach.detail: Treatment centres on manual therapy — mobilising and manipulating joints, nerves and muscles — to correct the postural and movement problems behind your symptoms and support early healing. You may be asked to do simple exercises at home or at work to hold those corrections between sessions.

approach.title: Rehabilitation and prevention
approach.summary: A specific exercise programme so the problem does not come back.
approach.detail: We address the factors that contributed to the problem in the first place. Your physiotherapist designs a specific exercise programme to improve muscle function, which may include our Pilates classes, run by specialist physiotherapists. Where it is relevant you will also get training and office ergonomics advice. The aim is for you to manage the condition independently.
